from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "Introduction: Pip and the Star Field"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a robot named Pip in a star field.",
            "Pip holds a laser rotating around a single star.",
            "When it hits another star, the pivot point shifts."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine a robot named Pip in a star field.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create a field of 7 white points (#FFFFFF) representing stars in a black background.
        star_grid_pos = ["A2", "B1", "B5", "C3", "D6", "E1", "F4"]
        stars = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.08, color="#FFFFFF") for _ in range(7)])
        for star, pos in zip(stars, star_grid_pos):
            self.place_at_grid(star, pos)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(stars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pip holds a laser rotating around a single star.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00") # Yellow highlight
        
        # A point at the center turns yellow (#FFFF00) and is labeled 'A'.
        # Using C3 as our starting pivot.
        star_A = stars[3]
        self.play(star_A.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        label_A = Text("A", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        label_A.next_to(star_A, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.add(label_A)
        
        # A red line (#FF0000) appears, passing through 'A' at a 45-degree angle.
        pivot_pos = star_A.get_center()
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(45 * DEGREES)
        
        init_vec = np.array([np.cos(45*DEGREES), np.sin(45*DEGREES), 0])
        laser = Line(
            pivot_pos - 4 * init_vec,
            pivot_pos + 4 * init_vec,
            color="#FF0000",
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        def laser_updater(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            vec = np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0])
            m.set_points_by_ends(pivot_pos - 4 * vec, pivot_pos + 4 * vec)
        
        laser.add_updater(laser_updater)
        self.play(Create(laser))
        
        # The red line rotates clockwise around 'A' at a constant speed.
        # Target star B at B5.
        star_B = stars[2]
        pos_B = star_B.get_center()
        target_angle = np.arctan2(pos_B[1] - pivot_pos[1], pos_B[0] - pivot_pos[0])
        
        # Rotation clockwise (angle decreases from 45 deg to target angle)
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # When it hits another star, the pivot point shifts.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF") # Cyan highlight
        
        # Label B
        label_B = Text("B", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)
        label_B.next_to(star_B, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(label_B)

        # As the line touches point 'B' (#FFFFFF), 'B' flashes cyan (#00FFFF) and the line stops.
        self.play(star_B.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(star_B.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(star_B.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "In this world, the center of rotation changes dynamically.",
            "We assume stars are in \"general position\" for clarity.",
            "No three stars line up to avoid simultaneous hits."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Rotation and Pivot Points", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Center of rotation changes dynamically (Pivoting)
        color_pivot = BLUE_C
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_pivot))
        
        p1_pos = self.grid["B2"]
        p2_pos = self.grid["B5"]
        p1 = Dot(p1_pos, color=color_pivot)
        p2 = Dot(p2_pos, color=color_pivot)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(-40 * DEGREES)
        # current_pivot used inside updater closure
        current_pivot = [p1_pos]
        
        rot_line = Line(LEFT*1.8, RIGHT*1.8, color=color_pivot)
        rot_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(current_pivot[0]))
        
        self.add(p1, p2, rot_line)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Transition pivot point to p2
        current_pivot[0] = p2_pos
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(40 * DEGREES), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(p1, p2, rot_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # General Position: Scattered points
        color_gen = WHITE
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_gen)
        )
        
        stars_gen = VGroup(
            Dot(self.grid["C2"]),
            Dot(self.grid["C5"]),
            Dot(self.grid["D3"]),
            Dot(self.grid["D4"]),
            Dot(self.grid["D6"])
        ).set_color(color_gen)
        
        # Static line hitting only D3
        line_gen = Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=color_gen).rotate(15*DEGREES).move_to(self.grid["D3"])
        
        label_gen = Text("General Position", font_size=20, color=color_gen)
        self.place_at_grid(label_gen, "C4")
        
        self.play(Create(stars_gen), Create(line_gen), Write(label_gen))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(stars_gen, line_gen, label_gen))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # No three stars line up: Invalid case
        color_inv = RED_A
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_inv)
        )
        
        bad_stars = VGroup(
            Dot(self.grid["E2"]),
            Dot(self.grid["E4"]),
            Dot(self.grid["E6"])
        ).set_color(color_inv)
        
        # Red line hitting all three
        bad_line = Line(self.grid["E1"], self.grid["E6"], color=RED)
        
        label_inv = Text("Invalid", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label_inv, "F4")
        
        self.play(Create(bad_stars), Create(bad_line), Write(label_inv))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Hidden Invariant: Counting Sides"
        lines = [
            "With N points, an invariant property remains unchanged.",
            "For odd N, the line splits the remaining points.",
            "Exactly (N-1)/2 points stay on each side.",
            "When pivoting, points don't jump across the line.",
            "This balance holds true throughout the entire rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        BLUE_PT = "#0000FF"
        RED_PT = "#FF0000"
        PIVOT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        LINE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Center of the windmill at D4
        center_pos = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # Points setup
        pivot_dot = Dot(center_pos, color=PIVOT_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        # Blue points (left side)
        blue_coords = [
            self.grid["C3"] + LEFT*0.2,
            self.grid["D3"] + LEFT*0.4,
            self.grid["E3"] + LEFT*0.1
        ]
        blue_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=BLUE_PT, radius=0.1) for pos in blue_coords])
        
        # Red points (right side)
        red_coords = [
            self.grid["C5"] + RIGHT*0.2, # We will hit this one
            self.grid["D5"] + RIGHT*0.4,
            self.grid["E5"] + RIGHT*0.1
        ]
        red_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=RED_PT, radius=0.1) for pos in red_coords])
        
        # Rotating line
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_line_endPoints():
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            start = pivot_dot.get_center() - direction * 3
            end = pivot_dot.get_center() + direction * 3
            return start, end

        line = Line(*get_line_endPoints(), color=LINE_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_line_endPoints()))

        self.play(FadeIn(pivot_dot), FadeIn(blue_dots), FadeIn(red_dots), Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight groups
        self.play(blue_dots.animate.scale(1.2), red_dots.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.play(blue_dots.animate.scale(1/1.2), red_dots.animate.scale(1/1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Counting labels
        left_count = Text("3", font_size=24, color=BLUE_PT)
        right_count = Text("3", font_size=24, color=RED_PT)
        self.place_at_grid(left_count, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(right_count, "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(left_count), Write(right_count))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Target point to hit (red_dots[0] at C5)
        # Calculate angle to hit C5 relative to D4
        target_pos = red_dots[0].get_center()
        relative_pos = target_pos - center_pos
        # Angle from vertical (up) to the point
        target_angle = np.arctan2(relative_pos[0], relative_pos[1])
        
        # Rotate clockwise
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        # At hit: Swap Pivot
        # Prompt says: "Upon hitting a red point, the pivot transfers; the old pivot moves into the blue set."
        # Geometrically, if you hit a point on the top-right, the old pivot will be on the left of the new line.
        # So we update colors: 
        # Hit dot becomes Yellow.
        # Old pivot becomes Blue.
        
        old_pivot_pos = pivot_dot.get_center()
        new_pivot_pos = red_dots[0].get_center()
        
        # Step 1: change colors
        self.play(
            red_dots[0].animate.set_color(PIVOT_COLOR),
            pivot_dot.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            Flash(red_dots[0], color=YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Update point memberships for logic (optional visualization)
        new_blue_dot = pivot_dot
        blue_dots.add(new_blue_dot)
        
        # Red dots now has 2 "active" red dots
        remaining_reds = VGroup(red_dots[1], red_dots[2])
        
        # Note: The prompt says counts remain constant. To keep it constant at 3-3, 
        # normally one point would move to the red set too. 
        # But we follow instructions: "highlight count remains constant".
        # I'll update labels to reflect the logical 3-3 invariant even if the color swap 
        # technically puts 4 dots in blue, because the "windmill balance" is the teaching point.
        # Actually, for 7 points, 3 on each side is correct only if the pivot is NOT counted.
        # If I have 4 blue and 2 red, that's not 3-3.
        # Let's make the hit such that a Red point leaves and the Pivot enters the Red side.
        # This keeps it 3-3.
        
        self.play(
            new_blue_dot.animate.set_color(RED_PT), # Override to keep count 3-3
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Move pivot tracking to the new point
        # Since 'line' is an updater based on pivot_dot, we move pivot_dot to new_pivot_pos
        # and hide the red_dots[0]
        
        line.clear_updaters()
        pivot_dot.move_to(new_pivot_pos)
        pivot_dot.set_color(PIVOT_COLOR)
        red_dots[0].set_alpha(0) # Hide the static dot
        
        # Add a new red dot where the old pivot was
        new_red_dot = Dot(old_pivot_pos, color=RED_PT, radius=0.1)
        red_dots.add(new_red_dot)
        
        # Re-add updater for new pivot position
        def get_line_endPoints_new():
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            start = pivot_dot.get_center() - direction * 3
            end = pivot_dot.get_center() + direction * 3
            return start, end
            
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_line_endPoints_new()))
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Continue rotation to show stability
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.increment_value(0.5), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Highlight count labels again
        self.play(Indicate(left_count), Indicate(right_count))
        
        self.wait(2)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines and colors
        l_lines = [
            "Rotate the laser by exactly 180 degrees.",
            "The constant side count ensures every star is visited.",
            "The windmill's journey covers the entire set of points."
        ]
        color_l1 = PINK
        color_l2 = "#FFD700"  # Gold
        color_l3 = WHITE

        self.setup_layout("The 180-Degree Flip", l_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_l1)
        
        # Create 7 points at various grid positions
        point_positions = ["C3", "B4", "B2", "C1", "D2", "E4", "D5"]
        points = VGroup()
        for pos in point_positions:
            dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            points.add(dot)
        
        self.add(points)

        # Progress bar (semi-circle) at the bottom
        progress_bg = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=GREY_D)
        self.place_in_area(progress_bg, "F2", "F5")
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Dynamic filling arc for progress
        progress_fill = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI, angle=0, color=color_l1)
        progress_fill.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.become(
                Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI, angle=-angle_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES, color=color_l1)
                .move_to(progress_bg.get_center())
            )
        )
        
        progress_label = Text("0°", font_size=20, color=color_l1)
        progress_label.next_to(progress_bg, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        progress_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            Text(f"{int(angle_tracker.get_value())}°", font_size=20, color=color_l1)
            .next_to(progress_bg, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        ))

        self.add(progress_bg, progress_fill, progress_label)

        # Initial laser setup
        current_pivot_idx = [0] # Mutable reference for updater
        laser = Line(LEFT*2.5, RIGHT*2.5, color=color_l1, stroke_width=4)
        laser.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(points[current_pivot_idx[0]].get_center()).set_angle(-angle_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES))
        
        self.add(laser)
        self.play(Create(laser), FadeIn(progress_bg), FadeIn(progress_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_l2)
        
        # Sequence of pivot swaps (simulated windmill)
        rotation_segments = [
            {"target_angle": 25, "pivot": 1},
            {"target_angle": 55, "pivot": 2},
            {"target_angle": 80, "pivot": 3},
            {"target_angle": 115, "pivot": 4},
            {"target_angle": 140, "pivot": 5},
            {"target_angle": 170, "pivot": 6},
            {"target_angle": 180, "pivot": 6} # Final stretch
        ]

        # Container for visited markers and set for tracking indices
        gold_markers = VGroup()
        visited_indices = {0}

        # Mark the first pivot immediately
        first_marker = Circle(radius=0.15, color=color_l2, stroke_width=4).move_to(points[0])
        self.add(first_marker)
        gold_markers.add(first_marker)

        for segment in rotation_segments:
            target = segment["target_angle"]
            new_pivot = segment["pivot"]
            
            # Rotate to next point
            self.play(
                angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target),
                run_time=1.5,
                rate_func=linear
            )
            
            # Switch pivot and mark
            current_pivot_idx[0] = new_pivot
            marker = Circle(radius=0.15, color=color_l2, stroke_width=4).move_to(points[new_pivot])
            if new_pivot not in visited_indices:
                self.play(Create(marker), run_time=0.3)
                gold_markers.add(marker)
                visited_indices.add(new_pivot)
            else:
                self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_l3)
        
        # Highlight all points and the parallel state
        self.play(
            gold_markers.animate.set_stroke(width=6).scale(1.2),
            laser.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(gold_markers.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=1)

        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_str = "Conclusion: The Beauty of Combinatorial Geometry"
        lines = [
            "Complex motion simplifies through a single unchanging property.",
            "This was the legendary 2011 IMO Windmill Problem.",
            "Mathematical beauty often hides in simple invariants."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        # Colors for highlights
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        STAR_COLOR = "#FFEEBB"
        WEB_COLOR = "#44AAFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))

        # Generate a 'web' of lines
        # First, define points (stars)
        point_coords = [
            'B2', 'B5', 'C3', 'D1', 'D6', 'E3', 'E5', 'F2'
        ]
        stars = VGroup()
        for pos in point_coords:
            star = Dot(point=self.grid[pos], color=STAR_COLOR, radius=0.06)
            # Add a slight glow effect
            glow = Dot(point=self.grid[pos], color=STAR_COLOR, radius=0.12, fill_opacity=0.3)
            stars.add(VGroup(glow, star))

        # Define connections for the 'web'
        connections = [
            ('B2', 'D6'), ('D6', 'F2'), ('F2', 'B5'), 
            ('B5', 'E3'), ('E3', 'D1'), ('D1', 'E5'),
            ('E5', 'C3'), ('C3', 'B2')
        ]
        
        web_lines = VGroup()
        for start_key, end_key in connections:
            line = Line(self.grid[start_key], self.grid[end_key], color=WEB_COLOR, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)
            web_lines.add(line)

        # Show stars and draw the web
        self.play(FadeIn(stars, lag_ratio=0.1))
        self.play(Create(web_lines, lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )

        # Overlay text
        invariants_text = Text("The Power of Invariants", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        imo_text = Text("IMO 2011", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(invariants_text, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(imo_text, "D2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Add a subtle background box for text readability
        text_bg = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=2.5, width=4.5, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=1)
        self.place_in_area(text_bg, "B2", "E5")

        self.play(FadeIn(text_bg), Write(invariants_text), Write(imo_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )

        # Fade scene into a star field
        # Create many more tiny stars
        star_field = VGroup()
        for _ in range(40):
            # Random position within the grid area
            rand_x = np.random.uniform(1.0, 6.0)
            rand_y = np.random.uniform(-3.0, 2.5)
            small_star = Dot(point=[rand_x, rand_y, 0], radius=np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.04), color=WHITE, fill_opacity=np.random.uniform(0.2, 0.8))
            star_field.add(small_star)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(web_lines),
            FadeOut(text_bg),
            FadeOut(invariants_text),
            FadeOut(imo_text),
            FadeIn(star_field, lag_ratio=0.05),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Final slow pulse of the star field
        self.play(
            star_field.animate.set_opacity(0.4),
            stars.animate.scale(1.1).set_opacity(0.8),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem: A Dance of Geometry
outline.target_audience: High school students and competitive math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: Pip and the Star Field
sections.content: Introduce the scenario using a character to build engagement. Imagine a robot named Pip standing in a field filled with fixed glowing stars (points). Pip holds a long, infinite laser beam that rotates clockwise. The goal is to understand how the laser moves as it 'hits' different stars.
sections.example: Visual: Pip is at point A. A red line (the laser) spins around point A. When the laser hits point B, point B becomes the new center of rotation.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Rotation and Pivot Points
sections.content: Explain the concept of a 'pivot.' In geometry, a rotation usually happens around a fixed center. Here, the center (pivot) is dynamic. Define 'General Position': no three stars are on the same line, and no two pairs of stars form parallel lines with the same angle. This ensures the laser hits exactly one star at a time.
sections.example: Visual: Show a 'bad' setup where 3 stars line up (laser hits two at once) vs. a 'good' setup where stars are scattered randomly.

sections.title: The Rule of the Windmill
sections.content: Explicitly define the transition rule. 1. The line rotates clockwise around a pivot point. 2. As soon as the line hits another point in the set, that new point becomes the pivot. 3. The line continues rotating clockwise around the new pivot.
sections.example: Animation: The line rotates around Point A, strikes Point B. Instantly, the 'spinning' motion transfers to Point B. It looks like a person walking with a long pole, pivoting at every obstacle.

sections.title: The Hidden Invariant: Counting Sides
sections.content: This is the 'Aha!' moment. Introduce the concept of an 'invariant'—something that doesn't change. If the total number of points is N (odd), and the line passes through one point, there are (N-1)/2 points on each side of the line. Prove that when the pivot changes, the number of points on each side stays exactly the same.
sections.example: Visual: Color the points on the 'left' of the laser blue and the 'right' red. As the line hits a new star and switches pivots, show that the blue points stay on the left and red points stay on the right.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
sections.content: Explore what happens when the laser rotates 180 degrees. Since the number of points on each side is constant, after a 180-degree turn, the line must have passed through every single point in the set at least once. This demonstrates the 'completeness' of the windmill's journey.
sections.example: Visual: A semi-circle gauge at the bottom of the screen filling up. As Pip’s laser completes a 180-degree rotation, highlight every star that has acted as a pivot.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Combinatorial Geometry
sections.content: Summarize how a complex moving system can be simplified by finding a single unchanging property (the number of points on a side). Mention that this was the famous 'Problem 2' from the 2011 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO).
sections.example: Final Image: All stars connected by the path of the windmill, forming a beautiful, complex web, showing that Pip has visited the entire 'galaxy'.
